chunks: What Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim narrated from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad al-Aḥmasī, from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Bajalī, who said:

I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, or wrote to him, about Saʿīd ibn Yasār: he had fallen from his camel and could not hold himself upright because of his abdomen. Should I perform the tawaf on his behalf and do the saʿy? He said: No; rather, leave him. If he recovers, he himself should make it up; otherwise, then you make it up on his behalf.

key_terms.قَضَى: performed later as compensation or make-up
key_terms.يَسْتَمْسِكُ: to hold oneself steady or remain upright

ai.seo_question: Can tawaf and saʿy be performed on behalf of an injured person who cannot complete them himself?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a sick or injured person who is unable to complete tawaf and saʿy. The Imam عليه السلام instructs that one should wait; if the person recovers, he must perform it himself, and if not, another may fulfill it on his behalf.
